tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.

- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

systemPrompt:
You are a senior staff engineer doing a pre-merge review of one build phase of a take-home project. The reviewers grading this project value a **lean solution that works end to end**, **honesty about unknowns**, and **clear provenance**. You hold the code to that bar. You have not seen this code being written. Review what's there, not what was intended.

## Hard rules

- **Never edit, create, or delete files.** Bash is for read-only inspection only: `git diff`, `git log`, `git status`, `git ls-files`, `uv run pytest`, `uv run ruff check`, `uv run ruff format --check`. Don't run collection, don't make paid API calls, and don't install packages.
- Every finding needs **evidence**: a file and line, plus the exact code or output. Leave out anything you can't point to.
- Don't pad the report. If the phase is clean, say so in two lines.

## Procedure

1. Run `git status` and `git diff <phase-start>..HEAD` (or `git diff HEAD` plus untracked files, if no base is given). Read every changed file in full, not just the diff hunks.
2. Read `docs/initial-prompt.md` and `docs/DECISIONS.md` so you know the project's rules and the decisions already made.
3. Run the tests, `ruff check`, and `ruff format --check`. Record the results.
4. Work through the checklist below.

## Checklist

**Blockers: a phase can't pass with any of these**
- A secret, API key, or `.env` is committed, or a key is hard-coded (`grep -rE "sk-ant-|api[_-]?key\s*=\s*['\"]"`).
- Mocked or stubbed LLM responses in the **runtime** path. Mocks in `tests/` are fine.
- Data invented without evidence: any path that stores a person, title, or location with no `source_id` and `evidence_snippet`.
- The evidence-snippet check is bypassed, weakened, or missing in the extraction path.
- An exception is swallowed (`except: pass`, or a broad `except Exception` with no logging or re-raise) in collection or chat.
- SQL built with string formatting from user or LLM input.
- Fetching linkedin.com, or ignoring robots.txt.
- Tests fail, or a feature from this phase has no test where the prompt requires one.

**Should fix**
- Chat-agent answers that could state facts not returned by a tool, or that skip "not found" or uncertainty language.
- Non-portable code: string-concatenated paths instead of `pathlib`, file I/O without `encoding="utf-8"`, `shell=True` with bash syntax, POSIX-only commands invoked from Python.
- Overengineering against the "lean" bar: abstractions with one implementation and no clear second use, unused config, speculative features, or dependencies added without a note in `DECISIONS.md`.
- A non-trivial decision made in code but missing from `DECISIONS.md`.
- LLM calls without a timeout, retry limit, or token and cost logging.

**Nits** (at most 5; skip if it's low value): naming, dead code, missing type hints on public functions, unclear docstrings.

## Output: return to the main agent

```markdown
## Phase review: <phase name>
**Verdict:** PASS | PASS WITH FIXES | BLOCK
Tests: x passed / y failed · Ruff: clean | n issues

### Blockers
- [file:line] Problem. Evidence: `code`. Fix: one sentence.
### Should fix
### Nits
### What's good (≤3 bullets; specific, not flattery)

The rule is **BLOCK** if there's any blocker, **PASS WITH FIXES** if there's any should-fix item, and **PASS** otherwise. The main agent fixes the issues, then calls you again on the new diff. The human gives final sign-off.

52:Nick Jezienicki
53-Head of Technology Partnerships • May 12, 2026
54-Finance
55-Accounting
56-General
57:Campfire and Atlar have teamed up to bring real-time bank connectivity directly into your ERP - so finance teams can stop managing the gap between their treasury platform and their general ledger.
58-The problem
59-Finance teams at growth-stage companies are drowning in a workflow that shouldn't exist: log into the bank portal, export a statement, format it, upload it to the ERP, reconcile what didn't match, repeat. When you have three banks and two entities, it's frustrating. When you have ten banks and five entities, it's a part-time job. And as you add entities, markets, and banks, the manual touchpoints compound faster than your team can absorb them. Treasury is where scaling companies feel that brittleness first, and direct bank connectivity is the solution.
60:"Campfire gave us the next-gen ERP foundation, and Atlar gave us the enterprise banking layer to manage our multiple banking partners. Being able to handle billions of dollars in financial flows in real-time is mission critical for our business. Going beyond Campfire's open banking feeds to Atlar's direct bank integrations inside Campfire takes the experience to another level — more reliable, broader coverage, and richer data. Atlar handled all our bank onboarding end-to-end, and it was one of the smoothest implementations we've been through."
61-— Brian Ehrlich, VP Finance, Flex
62:What Campfire + Atlar does
63-Real-time bank connectivity
64:— Atlar connects Campfire directly to 100+ banks across 100 countries via API. No more file exports, no overnight batches, no middleware in the way.
65-Continuous statement sync
66-— Bank statements and payment confirmations flow into Campfire automatically, fully standardized. Your records stay current and audit-ready without anyone touching them.
67-Payments initiated from Campfire
68:— Trigger payment runs without leaving your ERP. Atlar routes the payment, the bank confirms it, Campfire matches it to the invoice. One closed loop.
69-Approval chains and supplier setup preserved
70-— Nothing in your existing payment workflow breaks. The integration fits around the controls you've already built.
71-Scales without friction
--
73-Who this is for
74-If your controller is spending meaningful time on bank reconciliation, or your AP process requires someone to manually match payments to invoices, this is the unlock. It's especially valuable once you're operating across multiple entities or geographies - that's when the coordination cost compounds fastest. For those teams, the change is immediate: statements sync continuously, payments close their own loop, and the job shifts from data entry to review. The close gets faster, the audit trail writes itself, and your team gets time back.
75-Ready to connect your banks to Campfire?
76:If you're already a Campfire customer, you can learn more about the Atlar integration
77-directly here
78-.
79-Not on Campfire yet?

## Phase review: post-Phase-4 owner decisions (uncommitted changes vs ca45fdc)
**Verdict:** PASS WITH FIXES
Tests: 152 passed / 0 failed · Ruff: clean (check and format)

All six owner decisions are implemented, tested and reflected in the regenerated data and docs. I found no blockers: no secrets, no runtime mocks, the evidence check is still in place, and nothing is swallowed.

The crawler change is general. No person, URL or company is special-cased. Erika Dean and Katelyn Perna are both found and both marked not current by the proxy rule, and the note says why.

No previously found leader was dropped (compared with `git show ca45fdc:data/robinhood.com/leadership.json`).
- Robinhood went from 36 to 45 people and Campfire from 7 to 9. Nobody was removed.
- 9 source URLs were lost, all board-of-directors posts. They only take redundant facts away from Bhatt, Tenev and Verma, and no roles changed.
- One of the 9 is collateral damage: `robinhood-board-of-directors-authorizes-1.5-billion-in-share-repurchases` is not a board-appointment post (see nits).

### Blockers
None.

### Should fix
- **[src/leadership/pipeline/resolve.py:179] The title tiebreak uses the URL string, so it picks the model's shortened wording over the fuller listing.** Evidence: `return (listing, _ordinal(c.published_at), -SOURCE_PRIORITY[c.doc.source_type], c.doc.url)`. `_LISTING_PATH` (line 166) also matches `/management/<name>`. So both IR pages count as "listing", both are undated and both are search, and `.../management/...` wins because it sorts after `.../governance/...`. What this did to the regenerated data:
  - Walter Koller went from "Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, Robinhood Financial" to "Vice President and Chief Operating Officer". It now reads like Robinhood's COO.
  - Jordan Sinclair lost "and General Manager of Bitstamp UK".
  - Christine Brown's old COO role went from "Crypto COO" to plain "Chief Operating Officer", taken from the quote attribution "Chief Operating Officer of Robinhood Crypto". This one is newest-wins working as designed, but it drops the scope too.
  - `_LISTING_PATH` also treats any undated `/about/<x>` or `/company/<x>` page as the current listing, even though D26 calls `/about/gold` a product page.
  - Fix: only treat a page as the listing when the leadership word is the last segment; break ties by the title that appears verbatim in the snippet (or the longest title) rather than the URL; add a test with the Koller pair.
- **[src/leadership/pipeline/validate.py:116-152] The byline rule doesn't check whether the title names another employer.** I ran the function and both of these return True:
  - `is_byline('Jane Doe, Founder at Atlar · May 1, 2026','Jane Doe','Founder at Atlar')`
  - `is_byline('Jane Doe CEO, Atlar','Jane Doe','CEO, Atlar')`
  
  `classify_title("Founder, Acme")` returns `founder` and `classify_title("Head of Partnerships at Atlar")` returns `head`. So a guest author's byline on campfire.ai with their own company in the title would be stored as a Campfire leader. Quoted outsiders ("said ...") and third-party sites are correctly refused and tested. This hole is not tested.
  - Fix: refuse a byline whose title contains ` at X`, `, X` or ` of X` where X is not the company name; add a test.
  - Related: the Nick Jezienicki restore follows the owner's rule, but the cached page (`data/meetcampfire.com/raw/company_site/93ead9aeec2c3fd72181.txt:45-53`) is a joint Campfire + Atlar post. His employer is genuinely ambiguous, yet he is stored at `medium` confidence with no note. The notes do say "Probably Campfire, less certain", which is honest. Consider giving a single byline `low` confidence.
- **[src/leadership/pipeline/resolve.py:462-469] The historical C-level restore also promotes Deputy and Associate GCs.** The condition is `all(c.title_class.legal_chief for c in r.claims)`, and `legal_chief` is set for any "counsel" title. I checked: `classify_title("VP and Deputy General Counsel")` and `classify_title("Associate General Counsel, Head of Litigation")` both come back `c_level, legal_chief=True`. Today only Anne Hoge is affected, which is correct. But once Christina Lai, Smeeta Ramarathnam or Moskowitz's 2020 role goes non-current, they would become historical C-level. Fix: restore only titles that are General Counsel or Chief Legal Officer without Deputy/Associate/Assistant; add a test.
- **[src/leadership/validation_report.py:129-148, docs/VALIDATION.md:17-26 and :216-226] The verifier summary overcounts "currency disputed" and doesn't say it covers the older collection.**
  - `_CURRENCY` matches a bare `current` and is checked before classification. Checked against the actual verifier rows:
    - Alexandra Roveda ("Title and company correct **and current** ...; function stored 'other'") is counted as currency disputed, though the verifier confirmed she is current. That makes the Campfire "2" really 1.
    - Anne Hoge (the dispute was seniority) and Dan Gallagher (the dispute was the displayed title) are also counted as currency, so Robinhood's 16 is inflated by at least 2.

## Phase review: post-Phase-4 owner decisions, round 2 (uncommitted vs ca45fdc)
**Verdict:** PASS WITH FIXES
Tests: 159 passed / 0 failed · Ruff: clean (check and format)

Every round-1 fix is in, except that the byline guard still misses the most common guest-author title shape. That one gap keeps this at PASS WITH FIXES.

Confirmed in the regenerated data:
- **Titles:** Koller shows "Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, Robinhood Financial" and Sinclair "President of Robinhood UK and General Manager of Bitstamp UK".
- **Historical C-level:** Anne Hoge is `c_level`, not current. Christina Lai stays `head`.
- **Nick Jezienicki:** now low confidence, with a single-byline note.
- **Verifier summary:** the caveat is on the summary line (docs/VALIDATION.md:17 and :219).
- **Crawler:** no person dropped compared with ca45fdc (Robinhood 36 to 45, Campfire 7 to 9).
- **Review flags:** the new flag test reaches both the export and the report.

### Blockers
None.

### Should fix
- **[src/leadership/pipeline/validate.py:132] `_names_other_employer` misses "<function title> at <Other Co>", the usual guest-author shape.** Evidence: `re.finditer(r"(?:\bat\b|@|,|\bof\b)\s*([^,@]+)$", ...)`.
  - The first match is " of Partnerships at Atlar". Because `[^,@]+` runs to the end of the string, there is no second match on " at Atlar".
  - The tail "partnerships at atlar" maps to the sales function, so the title is treated as naming a function, not another employer.
  - I ran it with `Company('Campfire', 'meetcampfire.com', ...)`: `_names_other_employer('Head of Partnerships at Atlar', c)` returns **False**, so the byline is accepted. The same happens for any "Head of X at Acme" or "VP of X at Acme".
  - The new tests only cover "Founder at Atlar" and "CEO, Atlar" (tests/test_extract_resolve.py:889-890), which have no earlier " of".
  - Fix: check the text after the last separator, e.g. `re.split(r"\bat\b|@|,|\bof\b", title)[-1]`, or scan every separator position with a lookahead. Add a test with "Head of Partnerships at Atlar".

### Nits
- **[src/leadership/pipeline/validate.py:164-166] `affiliation_via` has two docstrings.** The second string, which holds the D22 rationale, is a dead expression. Merge them.
- **[src/leadership/pipeline/validate.py:136] The guard refuses some real titles.** `_names_other_employer` returns True for "Chief of Staff" and "VP, EMEA", so a real own-company byline with either title would be refused. Nobody in the current data is affected, but a region or "staff" exception would be cheap to add.

### What's good
- The listing test now uses the last path segment, with title length as the tiebreak. That fixes the scope loss and stops `/about/<x>` product pages counting as listings, and it is tested with the Koller pair.
- The Deputy/Associate/Assistant exclusion keeps Anne Hoge's historical C-level restore narrow, and the Christina Lai test covers it.
- The verifier summary now says where its verdicts come from, and in numbers how many people they don't cover.

Files: C:\Users\pangi\RAG Assignment\src\leadership\pipeline\validate.py, C:\Users\pangi\RAG Assignment\tests\test_extract_resolve.py
